newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Opp'n urges jobs push after rates cut.
newsitem.headline: Australian Opp'n urges jobs push after rates cut.

text.p: Australia's Labor opposition on Wednesday urged the government to seize the opportunity offered by the fifth interest rate cut in a year to boost job creation.
Opposition treasury spokesman Gareth Evans said the Liberal-National government must target 4.0 percent jobs growth at its special cabinet meeting on employment on Tuesday.

"The government must grasp this opportunity to capitalise on low inflation and low interest rates with a major jobs push," he said in a statement. The government has projected 2.0 percent employment growth, year average, in the fiscal year from July 1.
The Reserve Bank on Wednesday cut official cash rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.0 percent, the fifth such cut in a year.
Evans said Prime Minister John Howard and Treasurer Peter Costello had failed to honour their 1996 election promise to tackle unemployment.

"The Reserve Bank has played its part. Mr Howard and Mr Costello can no longer sit on their hands and wait for the (economic) cycle to deliver the faster growth Australians so desperately need," Evans said.
